claim.markdown_says: specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 23087-23093 place them at column 0 with no indentation: "a) a group data item that contains an occurs-depending table." / "b) an occurs-depending table." / "c) a data item that is subordinate to an occurs-depending table." / "If a VALUE clause is associated with the data item referenced by a DEPENDING phrase, that value is considered to be placed in the data item after the occurs-depending table is initialized. claim.why_it_matters: The list nesting is the only thing binding a)/b)/c) and the closing paragraph to general rule 6) of 13.18.63.4. At column 0 they read as free-standing top-level items between rule 6) and rule 7), so a reader or a rule-slicing tool can attach them to the wrong rule, or read the closing sentence as a general statement about all VALUE clauses rather than a rule scoped to occurs-depending tables. The transcription's own convention indents sub-items everywhere else in this subclause -- line 23071 is "   c) for all other items" under rule 4), and the a)/b) of rule 16) on page 553 are indented three spaces -- so this block is an isolated anomaly, not house style.

verdict.reasoning: Both observations are factually accurate, but the difference is leading whitespace only -- formatting, not content -- so it is rejected under the 'only page-break furniture / formatting' rule. (1) PDF verified by 300dpi render (E:/Temp/specrecon/v552/spec_p552.png, crop_top.png): the numeral '7)' sits at the outer margin and its body text one indent level right; 'a)', 'b)', 'c)' and the 'If a VALUE clause is associated...' paragraph all start at that inner body-text level, flush with the rule-6 continuation 'occurrence data item is set to the maximum number of occurrences...'. So yes, the print shows them as sub-items/continuation of rule 6). (2) Markdown verified by measuring leading spaces: lines 23087/23089/23091/23093 have lead=0 while 23067/23069/23071/23076 (rule 4) and 23125/23127 (rule 16) have lead=3. So the house-style inconsistency is real as described. (3) But NO CONTENT IS MISPLACED, MISSING, ALTERED OR REORDERED. All four blocks appear verbatim, character-for-character, in exactly the printed sequence: immediately after rule 6)'s trailing colon on p551 line 23080 and immediately before rule 7) at line 23095. The 'misplaced-content' kind is a misnomer -- the content is in precisely the right place. (4) The claim's premise that 'the list nesting is the only thing binding' these blocks to rule 6) is false on two counts. First, there is no markdown list nesting to lose: 'a)' is not a CommonMark list marker (only digit forms '1.'/'1)' are), and a paragraph indented 0-3 spaces renders identically to one at column 0 -- both the indented rule-4 sub-items and these unindented ones render as flat paragraphs, so the rendered output is unchanged. The three-space indent is raw-file cosmetics. Second, the binding survives without it: rule 6) ends 'is one of the following:' and the next content is the a)/b)/c) enumeration, so any slicing on the document's own numbered-rule boundaries (^\d+\)) places all four blocks inside rule 6). The mis-attribution scenario needs a tool anchored on '^[a-z])' at column 0, and such a tool would already fail on every correctly indented sub-item elsewhere in the file. (5) The claimed semantic risk does not hold: the closing sentence is self-scoping -- 'If a VALUE clause is associated with the data item referenced by a DEPENDING phrase, that value ... after the occurs-depending table is initialized' names the DEPENDING phrase and the occurs-depending table in its own condition, so it cannot be read as a general statement about all VALUE clauses regardless of indentation. (6) The cause is page-break furniture: the indent is lost exactly at the p551->p552 boundary where the extractor restarts, and is preserved on both sides (rule 4) on p551, rule 16) on p553). An implementer deriving 13.18.63.4 GR6 from the markdown gets identical semantics to one reading the PDF, so the discrepancy is not material.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. The a)/b)/c) items and the closing DEPENDING-phrase paragraph are transcribed verbatim and in the correct position between GR 6) and GR 7); only the three-space leading indent used elsewhere for sub-items is absent, an artifact of the p551->p552 extraction boundary. It renders identically in CommonMark (three-space indentation creates no list nesting, and 'a)' is not a list marker), the rule-6 binding is preserved by the enumeration's position after 'one of the following:' and before '7)', and the closing sentence is self-scoping to DEPENDING phrases. At most a cosmetic whitespace-consistency nit for the raw file, severity cosmetic, not structural.
